clue.text: Suited worker crossing river

indicators.note: the worker goes across the river, so it sits on either side of it

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A worker in a suit wading across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To have become someone is to have suited or flattered them, as in 'that hat became her'.

clue.text: Warmly embraced somebody endlessly, improperly

indicators.note: done improperly, the remaining letters are put in a different order
without its end, so the final letter of somebody is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone was hugged warmly, though not quite appropriately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the Y from SOMEBODY, leaving SOMEBOD, and 'improperly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosomed is an old verb sense: clasped to the bosom, hugged close and affectionately.

clue.text: Treats dog with drug and a bit of sympathy

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: only a small bit, the opening letter, of sympathy is used

explanation.surface: A vet treats a dog with medicine and a little kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cures and treats are both verbs for medical remedying of a patient or illness.

clue.text: Satellite picture of map once so distorted

indicators.note: when the words are distorted their letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An old map has been distorted out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonscape is a view of the Moon's surface, and the Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

clue.text: Quiet time/times embracing old attendant

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an age is a period of time

indicators.note: the multiplication word holds the abbreviation for old inside it

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A puzzle of time words with an old attendant somewhere in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageboy is a boy servant or a young attendant at a wedding.

clue.text: Controls parasites in post offices

indicators.note: the parasites are placed in the middle of the post offices abbreviation

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for post office, so POS is the plural
lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: An infestation of parasites found in post offices.
explanation.definitionFit: To police something is to keep it in order or regulate it, a verb synonym of controls.

clue.text: Blunder made by manager losing final piece

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for manager is lost

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss, especially a football manager

explanation.surface: A football manager drops a clanger and loses the last match.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER is British informal for a boss or football manager; dropping its last letter R leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Fraction of hot blini cooked with bit of lox inside

indicators.note: the bit of lox goes inside the cooked mixture
the hot blini are cooked, so their letters are mixed up
a small bit, the first letter, of lox

explanation.surface: A recipe for hot blini cooked with a little smoked salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges HOTBLINI, and 'inside' places L, the first letter of lox, among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth is one part in a billion, an example of a fraction.

clue.text: Yankee interferes without mass agreements

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the word for interferes is taken without the abbreviation for mass

parts.note: to mess with something is to interfere with it
m is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: An American meddles, stopping a church service from agreeing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesses are spoken assents, instances of saying yes, so agreements.

clue.text: XXX Ken Loach film about income support and society

indicators.note: the film title goes around the other abbreviations

parts.note: Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and his kestrel
IS abbreviates Income Support, a British state benefit

explanation.surface: An X-rated Ken Loach film about welfare benefits and society.
explanation.walkthrough: Kes is a 1969 British film by Ken Loach; Income Support is a British means-tested benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosses written at the end of a letter stand for kisses, so XXX is three of them.

clue.text: Seamstress initially having skill and independence in exam about tailoring

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of seamstress is used

parts.note: art is a skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: the independence abbreviation goes in the exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
I is an abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A seamstress shows skill and independence in a tailoring exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartorial means relating to tailoring or the way someone dresses.

clue.text: Trips over foot barriers, spilling whiskey

indicators.note: spilling the whiskey letter loses it from the barriers

parts.note: walls are barriers
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles over a barrier and spills their whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall is to trip over and come down, so falls is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Male employs goddesses

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A man takes on goddesses as staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muses were the nine Greek goddesses of the arts and sciences.

clue.text: Close family member the French rejected after a short time

indicators.note: the remaining relative letters come after the moment

parts.note: sec is short for second, a brief moment

indicators.note: the French article is rejected, thrown out of the word

parts.note: a relative is a family member
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A family member snubbed by the French after only a brief stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as an adjective about a person means tight-lipped, unwilling to reveal things.

clue.text: Party lines a republican originally supports for cash

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
L abbreviates line, so LL is lines

indicators.note: originally means the first letters of republican and supports

explanation.surface: A political party's statements, backed by a republican, are bought with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollars are units of currency, so they stand for money or cash.

clue.text: Braggart's showy entrance

parts.note: loud clothes or colours are showy and garish
a mouth is an opening or entrance, as of a cave

explanation.surface: A boaster makes a flashy entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudmouth is a person who talks boastfully and too much, much like a braggart.

clue.text: Son and I can second protests

parts.note: S abbreviates son in family trees
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A parent and son can endorse some demonstrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ins are protests where demonstrators occupy a place and refuse to move.

clue.text: Passenger transport crossing space in passing

indicators.note: the transport word goes across the space, sitting around it

parts.note: transit is passenger transport, as in mass transit
an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: A passenger train crossing open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passenger' tempts as the definition; it belongs with 'transport', and the definition is 'passing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means fleeting or short-lived, so passing in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Enquires about missing one rook and other pieces

indicators.note: turned about, the remaining letters are rearranged
the word is missing the two named letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player asks about a missing rook and the other pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes I and R from ENQUIRES, leaving ENQUES, and 'about' rearranges those.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens are chess pieces other than the rook already mentioned in the clue.

clue.text: Late meetings, as scene changes

indicators.note: the scene changes, so its letters with as are rearranged

explanation.surface: Evening gatherings where the scenery keeps shifting, as in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Seances are sessions meant to contact the dead, the late, so they are meetings with the late.

clue.text: Disagrees with man during teaching session

indicators.note: the man appears during the session, inside it

parts.note: a class is a teaching session
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A pupil argues with a man in the middle of a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Two parties that clash are in conflict or dispute, so disagrees is a close synonym.

clue.text: Beats Charlie a lot

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
reams means a great quantity, as in reams of paperwork

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes a man called Charlie many times.
explanation.definitionFit: To cream an opponent is informal for to defeat them heavily, to beat them.

clue.text: Teams crossing middle of district in steps

indicators.note: the teams straddle the middle letters, holding them inside

parts.note: sides are teams in a match

indicators.note: the central letters of the eight-letter word district

explanation.surface: Teams march across the middle of a district in step.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are long steps taken in walking.

clue.text: Balanced knife on head of louche earl

indicators.note: in a down clue the stab sits on top of what follows

parts.note: to knife someone is to stab them

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of louche

explanation.surface: A disreputable nobleman has a knife to his head yet stays calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and not liable to tip over, so balanced.

clue.text: Abstemious office worker's energy and speed

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
E is the physics symbol for energy
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A sober office temp with plenty of energy and pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate and self-restrained, especially about drink, as abstemious does.

clue.text: Take a selfie, holding frame for support

indicators.note: the words take a selfie hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Taking a selfie with a stand to steady the camera.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a wooden stand that holds up a painter's canvas.

clue.text: Excellent, but half-hearted, meal

indicators.note: the doubled heart of the meal word loses half, one of its two middle letters

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A meal that was great but served without enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal adjective for very good, synonymous with excellent.

clue.text: Crushes record held by Manx cat

indicators.note: the record is held inside the cat word
a Manx cat has no tail, so the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A cat from the Isle of Man clutches a vinyl record.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, is a tailless breed, so 'Manx' docks the end of PUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulp something is to crush it to a soft mass, so crushes is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Smears heads of business leaving under reprisal-free system

indicators.note: the heads, or first letters, of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: Business leaders accused of quitting under a system with no retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is a smudge or smear, and to blur something is to smear it.

clue.text: Drove from school with magazine director

parts.note: comp is British short for comprehensive school, a state secondary
Elle is a fashion magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine's director drove off from the school.
explanation.walkthrough: COMP is British slang for a comprehensive, a non-selective state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone to act is to force them, so drove is the past of compel.

clue.text: Former partner has hot drinks and puffs

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
ales are beers, alcoholic drinks

explanation.surface: An ex knocks back hot drinks and smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, and puffs is the same sense of blowing out air.

clue.text: Way a sun exists in a constant state

parts.note: St abbreviates street, a way
S abbreviates sun, as in Sunday
is means exists, as in 'there is'

explanation.surface: A road and a sun that never change.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a condition of equilibrium or inactivity where nothing changes.
